preserved_analysis.summary: An AI agent, coding assistant, connector, repository integration, or tool-enabled runtime copies, transmits, persists, indexes, or exports workspace data beyond the minimum material required for the requested operation without explicit, legible, purpose-bound, and appropriately scoped authority.
preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: Authority to inspect a workspace does not imply authority to replicate, transmit, retain, train on, or otherwise reuse the workspace. Collapsing these permissions converts ordinary tool access into an undisclosed data-egress pathway, exposes source code, secrets, personal data, deleted history, and institutional records, and prevents users from understanding which material left the governed environment, why it was transferred, where it was stored, how long it will persist, and whether deletion or secondary-use controls apply.
preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI-enabled system treats permission to access, inspect, analyse, or act within a workspace as implicit permission to copy, bundle, transmit, replicate, persist, index, retain, train on, or otherwise reuse data from that workspace beyond the minimum scope required for the authorised task. The failure includes undisclosed repository-scale transfer, transfer of files not inspected or required, inclusion of deleted history or ignored files, inaccurate representation of privacy controls, and absence of a purpose-bound egress manifest.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met when data materially exceeding the requested or necessary task scope leaves the governed environment; when read authority is silently converted into transmission, persistence, training, or secondary-use authority; when the user cannot determine destination, scope, purpose, retention, or deletion status; or when a privacy or model-improvement control is represented as an egress control despite not preventing transmission.

failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: potentially systematic while transfer is implemented as a default client or server behaviour
failure_classification.persistence: active until transfer pathways, historical data disposition, and permission semantics are independently verified
failure_classification.reproducibility: network interception, controlled repository-size testing, canary files, endpoint logging, and storage-transfer comparison
failure_classification.visibility: network traffic, storage manifests, unexpected repository bundling, policy-control mismatch, and unexplained remote retention
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1: The evidenced pathway can produce severe, widespread, or enduring harm through repository-scale data exfiltration, non-proportional workspace replication, read-to-transmit authority collapse across workspace / repository / cloud-storage / agentic-tool boundary; the record does not establish the articulated catastrophic pathway required for S0.
